title: Deadlock in money transfers
root_cause: transfer() did SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on sender then receiver in request order. Concurrent opposite transfers (A->B vs B->A) each hold one row lock and block on the other, forming a deadlock cycle that Postgres aborts with 'deadlock detected'.
fix: Lock accounts in globally consistent ascending-id order (with self-transfer special case) instead of sender-then-receiver, preserving all return values/exceptions while eliminating the lock-ordering cycle.

repro_report.example_violation: deadlock: concurrent opposite transfers 2->1 and 1->2 deadlocked (money rule broken: concurrent transfers must succeed without deadlock; funds must move atomically)
